clue.text: One leaving order for artillery

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so the 'one' is dropped from the word for order

parts.note: an ordinance is an authoritative order or decree
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone departs carrying instructions to fetch the big guns.
explanation.walkthrough: ORDINANCE loses its I to give ORDNANCE; the two words are easily confused in spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is the collective term for military guns and cannon, so it is a synonym for artillery.

clue.text: Work? Not I, spoilt for choice!

indicators.note: something spoilt is ruined and jumbled, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
the letters of not and I, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to work, saying they are spoilt for choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt for choice' is a stock phrase, so 'for' looks part of it; it is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of the alternatives available, so it is a synonym for a choice.

clue.text: Outlaw peer, odd as can be

indicators.note: 'as odd as can be' says the letters are made as strange as possible, that is, scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rogue nobleman is described as thoroughly eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are needed for the second D and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal of the Wild West kind, the same as an outlaw.

clue.text: A very angry upset worker in firm

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: mad means furious
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee in a company is furious and distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like the company the worker is in; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unshakeable in resolve, so it is a synonym of firm as an adjective.

clue.text: One may cast a shadow in Beijing plant

definitions.text: One may cast a shadow in Beijing
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a paper lamp of the kind hung in Chinese streets
second meaning: Physalis, whose papery orange husks look like small paper lamps

explanation.surface: Something in Beijing casts a shadow, apparently a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic description of a paper lamp; the second is the garden plant named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both the collapsible paper lamp and Physalis alkekengi, grown for its lantern-shaped seed cases.

clue.text: A female in posh car getting more reckless

indicators.note: one thing sits in another, so the car's letters go round the rest

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car
taken as written
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman driving a luxury car grows increasingly careless on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A and SHE go inside the two Rs of Rolls-Royce: R(A SHE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means hasty and heedless, so its comparative form describes someone acting with less caution.

clue.text: As found in vaccines radiographer brought over

indicators.note: brought over means turned back, so the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
the letters wanted are sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A radiographer has brought some vaccines over to the clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a conjunction; it is the chemical symbol, defining the element.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the periodic-table symbol for arsenic, element number 33.

clue.text: Doctor in Hoy rebuilt a health spa

indicators.note: the doctor goes inside the reworked island name
something rebuilt is put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor on the island of Hoy has rebuilt a health spa there.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoy is an island in Orkney, off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydro is a hotel or resort offering water cures, in other words a health spa.

clue.text: Took exception to being put on after opener's taken off

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and it is removed

parts.note: a show that is put on is presented

explanation.surface: Someone was offended at being made fun of once the opening act left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' sounds like being teased; it is staging a show. 'Opener' suggests a cricket batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter about it, so took exception to is a phrase meaning the same.

clue.text: End argument for as opposed to against?

parts.note: a goal is an end or aim
a difference is a disagreement or argument

explanation.surface: A debate's closing remark about the case for versus the case against.
explanation.walkthrough: In football league tables, goals for minus goals against gives the figure used to separate teams on equal points.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes exactly how the tie-breaking figure is calculated, scored set against conceded.

clue.text: Japanese dog biting contralto in opera

indicators.note: a mouth biting something holds it between the jaws, so one piece clamps round the other

parts.note: the Tosa is a Japanese fighting-dog breed
C is a standard abbreviation for contralto

explanation.surface: A Japanese dog nips a singer during a performance at the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tosa is a large mastiff-type breed from Japan, rarely seen outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera about a singer, her painter lover and the police chief Scarpia.

clue.text: Nickname for resolute men in club teams

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
sides are teams in a match

explanation.surface: A sports club gives its teams a nickname that celebrates their determination.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironsides was the name given to Oliver Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War, and before that to Cromwell himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was earned by the steadfast toughness of Cromwell's troopers, hence a label for resolute men.

clue.text: Use to perform surgery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to work or run a machine
second meaning: what a surgeon does in theatre

explanation.surface: An instruction on what something is for: it is used for surgical work.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both running a machine and cutting into a patient on the table.

clue.text: A President Ford car

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Abraham, sixteenth US president
second meaning: a luxury car brand owned by the Ford Motor Company

explanation.surface: Reads as 'a President Ford car', as if Gerald Ford had a car named after him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Ford' wants to be read together as Gerald Ford; split it after President.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was a US head of state, and Lincoln is the upmarket marque in Ford's range.

clue.text: Deceptively prim, I ran centre with accomplice

indicators.note: something presented deceptively is disguised, so the letters are rearranged out of recognition

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who looks respectable confesses to running a centre with a shady associate.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner in crime is a fellow wrongdoer, which is exactly what an accomplice is.

clue.text: Rude when drinking drop of vodka on the rocks

indicators.note: a drinker takes something inside, so one word swallows the letter

parts.note: insolent means rude

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the spirit is used

parts.note: the first letter of vodka

explanation.surface: Someone gets rude after drinking vodka on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' is the bar term for served over ice, but here it means financially wrecked. V goes inside INSOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is failing, and insolvent means unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: One of the crocks at races?

definitions.text: One of the crocks at races?

indicators.note: racing letters dash about and end up in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Wonders whether some old wreck has turned up at a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A crock is British slang for a broken-down old car; the whole clue both supplies the letters and describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock car racing uses battered old saloons that bash into each other, so each vehicle is a crock at the races.

clue.text: So craftier plot hatched in jungle

indicators.note: a plot that is hatched is devised and made up, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cunning scheme is devised deep in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot hatched' reads naturally as a conspiracy being planned, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jungle is dense equatorial woodland, the same habitat as tropical rainforest.

clue.text: At home, dance up in the air

parts.note: someone at home is in
the limbo is a dance under a lowered bar

explanation.surface: A party at home has dancers leaping into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in the air' sounds like jumping; it means undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan in limbo is unresolved and uncertain, the same as one left up in the air.

clue.text: In tears having spilt wine

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is crying after knocking over their wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Large hole in old car beginning to rust

parts.note: a crate is slang for a battered old vehicle

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of rust

explanation.surface: An old banger has a big hole where rust has started to eat through.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a big bowl-shaped cavity in the ground, as made by a meteor or bomb.

clue.text: Two lines of verse produced by associate, last in sonnet

parts.note: to couple is to join or associate

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of sonnet

explanation.surface: A pair of lines written by a colleague closes off a sonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Associate' looks like a noun for a colleague; it is the verb, meaning to link together.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of consecutive rhyming lines, and Shakespearean sonnets end with one.

clue.text: Very vital to resourceful tramps

indicators.note: the vitals are the inner organs, so the answer sits in the core of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Being resourceful is extremely important for people living on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very vital' reads as one phrase; split after Very, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as a prefix or adjective means extremely, the same as very.

clue.text: Snake, excellent specimen

definitions.meaning: second meaning: informal word for a first-rate example of something

explanation.surface: A collector praises a fine example of a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is dated British slang, related to 'a rattling good' story.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is called a rattler for its tail, and a rattler is also colloquially anything outstanding.

clue.text: Sailing boat can crossing a West Country river

indicators.note: a thing crossing another spans it, so the word for can stretches across the rest

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Tamar forms the border between Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A sailing boat is able to cross a river in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb 'is able to'; it is the word itself, split around the rest. The West Country is south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled vessel, often powered by sail.

clue.text: Incompetent writer rejected in it

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the last word of the clue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A useless author has had their work turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests a person, but here it is the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or ability, a direct synonym of incompetent.

clue.text: Cause of timeless crime?

indicators.note: read as time-less, it asks for the word that follows minus the usual one-letter abbreviation for time

parts.note: treason is the crime of betraying one's country

explanation.surface: Asks what motive could explain a crime that no clock can date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' is split as time-less: TREASON without its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the ground or motive behind something, so it can stand for a cause.

clue.text: Put off drinking tin, for bottle

indicators.note: a drinker takes something inside, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to deter is to put someone off
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Discouraged from drinking out of a tin, someone reaches for a bottle instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking' fits the picture of a tin of beer, which hides its role as the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a stoppered glass bottle into which wine or spirits are poured for serving.
